questions.explanation: The report says most candidates identified the vector quantity correctly. The slip was in the mass: some did not rearrange the equations for momentum and kinetic energy. Momentum has a direction, so it is the vector; energy and mass are scalars. For the mass, p = mv and E = ½mv<sup>2</sup>, which combine to E = p<sup>2</sup>/2m. So m = p<sup>2</sup>/2E = 60<sup>2</sup> / (2 × 90) = 20 kg. Answer: C. Option D has the right vector and the wrong mass. Write both equations down and eliminate v before you put numbers in.

Option B was the common wrong answer. The report says many candidates believed the Sun is the source of energy for geothermal and tidal resources. It is not. Geothermal energy comes from heat inside the Earth, nuclear fuel is mined from the ground and tidal energy comes from the gravitational pull of the Moon. Fossil fuels store energy that came from the Sun long ago, and waves are driven by wind, which the Sun heats. So the pair derived from the Sun is D. Sort each resource into Sun-powered or not before you look at the pairs.

Option C was the common wrong answer. Its statement is true, but it does not explain the observation: nothing is being radiated at your hand. A rod feels cold when it conducts thermal energy away from your skin quickly. Metal is a better thermal conductor than plastic: B.

Many candidates used 60° as the angle of incidence, which gives option B. The 60° in the question is between the ray and the surface of the block. Angles of incidence are measured from the normal, so i = 90 − 60 = 30°. The speeds give the refractive index: n = 3.0 / 2.0 = 1.5. Then sin r = sin 30° / 1.5 = 0.333, so r = 19°: A. Using 60° instead gives sin r = 0.577 and r = 35°, which is option B. Mark the normal on the diagram before you read any angle.

Most candidates saw that the image is virtual. Some chose C, thinking the image is inverted and on the right-hand side of the lens. Look at the rays after the lens: they spread apart, so they never meet on the right. A virtual image is where the rays appear to come from when you trace them back, so it is on the same side as the object, and here the spreading rays show the object is inside the focal length, which gives an upright image. Answer: D. A real image needs the rays to cross after the lens.

Many candidates chose D, 300 000 000 m/s, which is the speed of light. The report says they confused the speed of sound in air with the speed of light. Sound travels about a million times slower: roughly 330 m/s, so 300 m/s is the closest value. Answer: B. Learn the two speeds as a pair: sound about 330 m/s in air, light 3.0 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s.

Option A was the common wrong answer. The report says many candidates thought a magnetic field acts on a moving charge but not a stationary one because only a moving charge has an electric field. A stationary charge has an electric field too, so that cannot be the difference. What changes when a charge moves is that it makes its own magnetic field, and that field interacts with the field of the magnet to produce a force. A stationary charge has no magnetic field of its own. Answer: C.

Some candidates chose D. The report says they did not apply what they know about current in the series and parallel parts of a circuit. In the series part, the same current passes every point. At A, C and D that is the whole current from the battery. The parallel section splits it, and the p.d. is the same across both branches, so the branch with the larger resistance takes the smaller share. The 6 Ω branch carries one third of the current and the 3 Ω branch two thirds. B is in the 6 Ω branch, so the current is lowest there: B.

Most candidates saw that a thermistor was needed. Many then chose C, putting it at Y. The report says they did not work out that a thermistor's resistance falls as the temperature rises, so the p.d. across it falls too. The question wants the p.d. across Y to rise with temperature. Put the fixed resistor at Y and the thermistor at X. When the temperature rises, X's resistance falls, X takes a smaller share of the supply p.d., and Y takes a larger share: D.

Option D was the common wrong answer. The report says some candidates confused the features of the d.c. motor with those of an a.c. generator. A d.c. motor has a coil, a magnetic field and a split-ring commutator, which reverses the current every half turn so the coil keeps turning the same way. Slip rings belong to the a.c. generator. The question asks what is not part of the d.c. motor: B.

Some candidates chose D, upwards. The report says some confused the direction of the current, or used the right-hand rule instead of the left-hand rule. Beta particles are electrons, so they are negative, and conventional current points opposite to their motion. The beam travels to the right, so the current points left. Left-hand rule: first finger into the page for the field, second finger to the left for the current, and the thumb points down the page: A. Treating the beam as a current to the right gives D.

Many candidates chose B, 7600 m/s. The report says they divided Mercury's distance from the Sun by its orbital period instead of using the correct equation. Most converted 88 days into seconds correctly: 88 × 24 × 3600 = 7.6 × 10<sup>6</sup> s. Mercury travels once round a circle in that time, so the distance covered is the circumference: v = 2πr / T = 2π × 5.8 × 10<sup>10</sup> / 7.6 × 10<sup>6</sup> = 4.8 × 10<sup>4</sup> m/s: C. The wrong route, 5.8 × 10<sup>10</sup> / 7.6 × 10<sup>6</sup>, gives 7600 m/s, which is option B.

The report found that the wrong answers were spread across A, B and D, which suggests many candidates guessed. This one is recall. When the hydrogen in its core runs out, a star like the Sun expands into a red giant, then sheds its outer layers and the core remains as a white dwarf. Supernovae and neutron stars belong to the life cycle of much more massive stars. Answer: C.
